Are you running on docker? Or did you install the docker version of ES?
 
This line (126)
```
/usr/share/elasticsearch/bin/elasticsearch-env: line 126: syntax error near unexpected token `<'
```
should only be relevant in the docker distribution of Elasticsearch.
No, I'm running it in a LXC zone - so more or less like bare metal.

Thanks.

You paste lines 90-94 of your `elasticsearch-env` file for us?
For example, this is from my local tar install:
```
$ cat -n bin/elasticsearch-env | sed -n -e90,94p
    90
    91	ES_DISTRIBUTION_FLAVOR=default
    92	ES_DISTRIBUTION_TYPE=tar
    93	ES_BUNDLED_JDK=false
    94
```

Do you know how Elasticsearch was installed on this machine? `.deb` package (`apt-get`), or direct download?

The error points to you having a setup that thinks it's the docker install, and we'd need to work out why.

Also, to check on an alternative theory, can you provide the output of:

- `/bin/bash --version`

and

- `uname -a`

No problem:
```
 > cat -n /usr/share/elasticsearch/bin/elasticsearch-env | sed -n -e90,94p
    90	
    91	ES_DISTRIBUTION_FLAVOR=default
    92	ES_DISTRIBUTION_TYPE=deb
    93	ES_BUNDLED_JDK=true
    94	

> /bin/bash --version

There is NO WARRANTY, to the extent permitted by law.

> uname -a
Linux hellas 5.4.0-48-generic #52-Ubuntu SMP Thu Sep 10 10:58:49 UTC 2020 x86_64 x86_64 x86_64 GNU/Linux
```
@pugnascotia any thoughts here. As Tim says, the line in the script that's complaining shouldn't even be executing here given this is a DEB install.
I guess some underlying scripts are not POSIX compatible and explode.

I'm struggling to replicate this. Here's what I tried (more or less).

```shell
docker run -it --rm ubuntu:20.04 bash
cd
apt-get update
apt-get install wget vim
wget https://artifacts.elastic.co/downloads/elasticsearch/elasticsearch-7.10.2-amd64.deb
dpkg -i elasticsearch-7.10.2-amd64.deb
echo "xpack.security.enabled: true" >> /etc/elasticsearch/elasticsearch.yml
service elasticsearch restart
/usr/share/elasticsearch/bin/elasticsearch-setup-passwords interactive
```
Is POSIXLY_CORRECT env var set? Otherwise add to the profile or set it manually after you got attached to the zone.
Aha, setting `POSIXLY_CORRECT` triggers the problem. I'll look into this, but in the meantime you can work around this by unsetting the env var.

issue.title: Tweak elasticsearch-env script to work under posix

labels.name: :Delivery/Packaging
labels.description: RPM and deb packaging, tar and zip archives, shell and batch scripts

repository.name: elasticsearch
repository.description: Free and Open Source, Distributed, RESTful Search Engine

issue.body:
Closes #65980. Also closes #67097 and closes #66656.

The elasticsearch-env script used a bash feature called "process
substitution", which doesn't work when `POSIXLY_CORRECT` is set in the
environment (the construct doesn't even parse). Tweak the implementation
to use something that works under `POSIXLY_CORRECT`.

Also add a test to `ArchiveTests`, which fails without this fix, and
rework `DockerTests.test085EnvironmentVariablesAreRespectedUnderDockerExec`
since a couple of issues were open against it.
